claude.result:
**ASHFALL OUTPOST is complete** at `./game.html` (~1823 lines, single self-contained file, no external resources, no storage APIs, no `Math.random`/`Date.now`).

All 13 systems from the spec are implemented: seeded mulberry32 core loop with a fixed 9-step documented turn order, an 8×8 generated map with terrain-gated buildings and adjacency bonuses (condenser↔water, forge↔vent, etc.), two real production chains (ore→metal via Forge consuming power; ash→soil→food via Greenhouse consuming water) with storage caps and logged overflow, individual colonists with skill/fatigue/morale driving output, a 10-node research tree with prereqs, a 12-event weighted deck (4 with genuine multi-way tradeoffs) with cooldowns, a caravan with stockpile- and drift-based pricing, ashstorms with escalating severity/mitigation/repair, JSON save/load with field-level validation, win/lose/score conditions, a full tabbed UI with tooltips on every number, and a Dev panel with 23 test assertions and a deterministic 200-turn benchmark with a state hash.

One environment note: this session's Bash tool gates all `node`/code-execution commands behind an approval that never arrived (even `node --check`), so I couldn't run the file or the Dev-panel tests myself to get a live confirmation. Instead I did a full manual line-by-line read of the entire generated file, verified brace/paren/bracket balance (445/445, 1447/1447, 181/181), and hand-traced turn 1's production math against the actual formulas to confirm the economy behaves sensibly. That review caught and fixed three real issues along the way: a CSS class mismatch that silently killed the "available research" highlight, a missing color rule for "warn"-tagged log lines, and two spots where a colonist name loaded from a pasted save file would have gone unescaped into `innerHTML` (self-XSS risk) — all fixed. I'd still recommend opening the file in a browser yourself to click through it, since I couldn't do that final live check.
